speaker: GOD
text: It is not good for the man to be alone.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Seven times in chapter one, God looked at His world and called it good. In chapter two, for the first time, something is not good. And the people who first heard this lived in tents around a sanctuary. They would have noticed something about this garden. It looks like one.

speaker: READER
text: This is the account of the heavens and the earth when they were created, in the day that the LORD God made them.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Listen to the turn inside the verse. The heavens and the earth become the earth and the heavens, and the camera comes down from the sky to the ground.

speaker: GUIDE
text: And God now has a name. The LORD, in small capitals, stands for His covenant name. In chapter one He speaks and worlds appear. Here He stoops and works with His hands. He forms, breathes, plants, takes, places, commands, brings, closes and builds.

speaker: GUIDE
text: This is not a second, competing creation story. It is a close up of the sixth day, and Jesus quotes both chapters together as one word from the Creator.

speaker: READER
text: Now no shrub of the field had yet appeared on the earth, nor had any plant of the field sprouted, for the LORD God had not yet sent rain upon the earth, and there was no man to cultivate the ground.

speaker: READER
text: But springs welled up from the earth and watered the whole surface of the ground.

speaker: GUIDE
text: The scene opens with what is missing. No shrub, no plant, no rain, and no man to cultivate the ground. Every lack is about to be met.

speaker: READER
text: Then the LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living being.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Formed is the potter's verb, the word for hands shaping clay. Isaiah says it plainly:

speaker: READER
text: we are the clay, and You are the potter,

speaker: GUIDE
text: The nations also told of humans made from clay, as servants to spare the gods their labour. Genesis is different. This man is given a garden, good food and meaningful work, and God's own breath.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Man, adam, is taken from the ground, adamah. We are earthy creatures, given dignity only by the breath of God.

speaker: READER
text: the breath of the Almighty gives me life,

speaker: READER
text: And the LORD God planted a garden in Eden, in the east, where He placed the man He had formed.

speaker: READER
text: Out of the ground the LORD God gave growth to every tree that is pleasing to the eye and good for food. And in the middle of the garden were the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Eden means delight. It is a garden of God's own planting, the first place where God dwells with man.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Notice the two trees in the middle. They are placed carefully, with the man, the woman and the command, so that the next chapter can test each one.

speaker: READER
text: Now a river flowed out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it branched into four headwaters:

speaker: READER
text: The name of the first river is the Pishon; it winds through the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.

speaker: READER
text: And the gold of that land is pure, and bdellium and onyx are found there.

speaker: READER
text: The name of the second river is the Gihon; it winds through the whole land of Cush.

speaker: READER
text: The name of the third river is the Tigris; it runs along the east side of Assyria. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.

speaker: GUIDE
text: The geography is deliberately real and deliberately beyond reach. Every Israelite knew the Tigris and the Euphrates. The Pishon and the Gihon cannot be identified with certainty.

speaker: GUIDE
text: And in the ancient world, the dwelling of a god was a place of abundant water. Here a river flows out from the place where God dwells, to water the whole world.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Now look at the camp the first hearers lived in.

speaker: GUIDE
text: For Israel, the garden looked like a sanctuary. Its entrance faces east, as the tabernacle's did. Gold and onyx were the materials of the priestly garments, and two onyx stones, engraved with the tribes' names, sat on the high priest's shoulders.

speaker: GUIDE
text: In the next chapter God walks in the garden, the same form of the verb He uses when He promises Israel:

speaker: READER
text: I will walk among you and be your God,

speaker: GUIDE
text: Israel's worship was, in part, a memory of Eden.

speaker: READER
text: Then the LORD God took the man and placed him in the Garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Cultivate and keep. The first verb means to work or serve, and is the ordinary word for serving God in worship. The second means to guard and keep, the word for keeping God's commands.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Together they describe the Levites in the tabernacle. Adam's work is farming, but it is also priestly service in the place where God dwells.

speaker: GUIDE
text: A keeper of a sanctuary needs one more thing. A word from the One who lives there.

speaker: READER
text: And the LORD God commanded him,

speaker: GOD
text: “You may eat freely from every tree of the garden,

speaker: GOD
text: but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil; for in the day that you eat of it, you will surely die.”

speaker: GUIDE
text: Listen to the order. The command opens with permission, every tree of the garden, and only then sets one limit. God's commands are not the grudging rules of a jealous master, but the boundaries of a good home.

speaker: GUIDE
text: And the warning is plain. God does not hide the consequences of disobedience. His word defines what is good and what is evil, and life depends on trusting it.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Whatever the knowledge of good and evil means exactly, the heart of the matter is trust: whether the man will receive it from God's word, or seize it on his own terms.

speaker: GUIDE
text: So the garden has everything. Food, beauty, work, and a word to live by. And then God Himself says that something is missing.

speaker: READER
text: The LORD God also said,

speaker: GOD
text: “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make for him a suitable helper.”

speaker: GUIDE
text: The first thing in the Bible called not good. And it is God Himself who names the lack, before the man does.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Helper is ezer, and Scripture uses that word most often of God Himself.

speaker: READER
text: My help comes from the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth.

speaker: GUIDE
text: It speaks of strength brought alongside, never of someone lesser. Suitable means one who stands face to face with him, his match.

speaker: READER
text: And out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field and every bird of the air, and He brought them to the man to see what he would name each one. And whatever the man called each living creature, that was its name.

speaker: READER
text: The man gave names to all the livestock, to the birds of the air, and to every beast of the field. But for Adam no suitable helper was found.

speaker: GUIDE
text: God brings the animals to the man to see what he would name each one, and honours his choices. But none of them stands face to face with him.

speaker: READER
text: So the LORD God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep, and while he slept, He took one of the man’s ribs and closed up the area with flesh.

speaker: READER
text: And from the rib that the LORD God had taken from the man, He made a woman and brought her to him.

speaker: GUIDE
text: The deep sleep is the same sleep that falls on Abram before God makes covenant with him. God works while the man is passive.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Rib can mean side, a builder's word used of the tabernacle's sides. And made is literally built. God builds the woman as a builder raises a house, and then He Himself brings her to the man.

speaker: READER
text: And the man said: “This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called ‘woman,’ for out of man she was taken.”

speaker: GUIDE
text: These are the first recorded human words in the Bible, and they are poetry. Man and woman, ish and ishshah, sound alike. Bone of my bones is the language of family.

speaker: READER
text: For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and they will become one flesh.

speaker: GUIDE
text: The narrator steps out of the story to apply it to every marriage after it. To be united is to cling or hold fast, the word Ruth uses of Naomi, and the word Moses uses of Israel and God:

speaker: READER
text: Hold fast to Him,

speaker: GUIDE
text: Marriage is a loyalty chosen and kept, not only a feeling. This chapter was written to shape Israel's homes.

speaker: READER
text: And the man and his wife were both naked, and they were not ashamed.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Naked, and not ashamed. The line closes the scene and sets up the next one. Every gift in this chapter is about to be tested.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Paul quotes this chapter and names Jesus as the last Adam.

speaker: READER
text: The first man Adam became a living being; the last Adam a life-giving spirit,

speaker: GUIDE
text: Adam was placed in a garden to serve and guard it, and given one word to keep. He failed at every point. Christ comes as the obedient Man who serves His Father perfectly.

speaker: GUIDE
text: John frames the passion with gardens. Jesus is arrested in a garden, buried in a garden, and on Easter morning Mary thinks He is the gardener. In a sense she is right.

speaker: GUIDE
text: That evening He breathes on His disciples, as God breathed into the first man, and says:

speaker: READER
text: Receive the Holy Spirit,

speaker: GUIDE
text: And Paul says the one flesh union was always pointing beyond itself.

speaker: READER
text: This mystery is profound, but I am speaking about Christ and the church,

speaker: GUIDE
text: When chapter three comes, each gift in this garden is damaged. The ground is cursed, work becomes toil, the marriage is strained, shame replaces nakedness without shame, and the way to the tree of life is barred.

speaker: GUIDE
text: But the prophets kept the garden alive. They promised a people in the desert that God

speaker: READER
text: will make her wilderness like Eden and her desert like the garden of the LORD,

speaker: GUIDE
text: And the Bible ends with Eden restored and surpassed. The river of the water of life flows from the throne of God and of the Lamb, and the tree of life stands on either side of it.

speaker: READER
text: eat from the tree of life in the Paradise of God,

speaker: GUIDE
text: The garden has become a city, but it is still a home where God and His people live together.

speaker: GUIDE
text: We are dust that breathes because He breathed. Every good gift, food, work, beauty, marriage and friendship, comes from His hand, and even His limits are a form of His care.

speaker: GUIDE
text: You were formed from dust and given life by God's breath. How does remembering that change how you see your worth today?

speaker: GUIDE
text: One tree, one word, and a man and a woman who trust it. In the next chapter, another voice speaks in the garden, and the first question it asks is about what God said.
